children: The decision to keep Malaysia's policy rate unchanged at 2.75% reflects the central bank's confidence in the economy's resilience, AmBank economists say in a note. The central bank believes current monetary settings can support robust growth while keeping inflation manageable, despite geopolitical tensions and elevated global commodity prices, they note. BNM expects economic growth to exceed 5% in 2026, while inflation is forecast to rise in 2027 as global cost pressures persist. However, AmBank says a rate hike would be premature given mounting global risks and manageable inflation, partly due to government subsidies. The central bank is likely to remain data-dependent and wait for greater clarity before tightening, it adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
